sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and static setting
sections.what: Brings in the data sources and file tools, and marks this route as fully static so it is produced at build time.
sections.why: The static setting keeps the bundle from being recalculated on every visit.
sections.watch_out: Removing the static setting makes the response compute on each request, which changes how it is served.

sections.name: readTour
sections.title: Reads one build's walkthrough file
sections.what: Opens the walkthrough file in a project's media folder and returns it as data, or nothing if the file is missing or broken.
sections.why: The walkthrough is written after screens are captured, so it lives in its own file rather than in the code.
sections.watch_out: A broken file fails silently, so a walkthrough can disappear with no error.

sections.name: GET
sections.title: Assembles the full home bundle
sections.what: Produces the single response the home page reads, combining the brain map, roles with photos and scenes, and builds with screenshots, videos and walkthroughs.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond its header; gathering the data in one place means the page makes one request.
sections.watch_out: A new field added to a data file will not reach the page unless it is also added in this function.

summary: Builds the data for the home page as one static JSON response that holds the brain map, the roles with photos and scenes, and the AI builds with their screens and walkthroughs.
purpose: Gives the home page one bundle of content so it does not have to assemble it from many sources.
why: Likely reason: the site is built as static files, so this bundle is produced once at build time instead of on every visit. The header comment says it is generated from the site's own data at build time.
how: 1) Reads the brain regions, nodes and fact links. 2) Builds the list of roles with their memory photos and scenes. 3) Builds the list of projects with screenshots, videos and walkthroughs read from each project folder. 4) Returns the three parts together as one JSON response.
inputs: The brain, battles, assets, projects and geo place data, plus an optional tour.json file in each project's media folder.
outputs: A JSON object with three parts: brain, roles and builds.
risks: A missing or broken tour.json is silently treated as no walkthrough. Image paths have their leading slash removed, so a change in path format breaks images. The response is fixed at build time, so data changes need a rebuild.
debug: If the home page shows missing data, open the generated response and see which part is empty. If a walkthrough is missing, check that tour.json exists in the matching project folder and is valid JSON. If images fail, check the paths in the data. Rebuild after editing data.
